learning_outcomes.text: Provide the basic concepts for understanding the operation and use of the most important turbomachines.

Knowledge of the laws of physics (mechanics and thermodynamics) relevant to the field of industrial engineering, and understanding of the role of such laws in the formulation of models representative of tangible reality.
Knowledge of thermodynamics and fluid dynamic phenomena, as well      as the models for representing them.
Knowledge of systems and machines for energy production and conversion, with particular reference to turbomachinery.
The ability to apply one's knowledge to solve turbomachinery-related problems by interpreting and using the laws that govern them.
The ability to choose and apply appropriate analytical, modeling, and experimental methods to study and design fluid machines, evaluating their performance.
Ability to analyze data and information, compare different solutions, and arrive at applicative engineering solutions.

Ability to communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions within the engineering field, presenting them clearly according to standard methods, and making use of graphs and tables where necessary.
Ability to acquire knowledge in the area of turbomachinery.
Ability to learn through practical exercises on real case studies.
Ability to understand and interpret the basic principles of turbomachinery design, their operation, and their use.
Ability to study, describe, and predict the physical behaviour of fluids.

Knowledge of the laws of physics (mechanics and thermodynamics) relevant to the field of industrial fluid dynamics, and understanding of the role of such laws in the formulation of models representative of tangible reality.
The ability to apply one's knowledge to solve fluid dynamics problems, in successive applicative engineering courses, by interpreting and using the laws that govern them.
Ability to analyze data and information using known tools, compare different solutions, and arrive at applicative solutions.

Ability to communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions within the engineering field, presenting them clearly, according to standard methods, and making use of graphs and tables where necessary.
Ability to acquire knowledge in fluid mechanics.
Ability to learn through practical exercises on real case studies.
Ability to understand and interpret the basic principles of aerodynamic design.

syllabus_topics: INTRODUCTION: Definition of fluid, integral and differential analysis methods
BASIC CONCEPTS: Flow as a continuum, flow and stress field, viscosity and Newtonian fluid
FLUID STATICS: Basic equations and buoyancy
BASIC EQUATIONS AND CONTROL VOLUME METHOD: Integral equations of continuity, momentum and energy
DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS FOR A FLUID FLOW: Continuity Equation, flow field, momentum end energy equation
INCOMPRESSIBLE INVISCID FLOW: Basic Equations , Euler Equations, Bernoulii Equation, total quantities
INTERNAL INCOMPRESSIBLE VISCOUS FLOW: Laminar and turbulent flows in pipes, losses and Moody diagram
EXTERNAL INCOMPRESSIBLE VISCOUS FLOW: Concept of laminar and turbulent boundary layer, transition, integral equation of the boundary layer, lift and drag
COMPRESSIBLE FLOW: Sound speed and Mach number. Basic equation of one-dimensional compressible flow, Fanno and Rayleigh line

assessment_methods.method: Oral examination with brief engineering problem (Fluidynamic module)

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on an oral examination for the Turbomachinery module and an oral examination combined with solving a brief engineering problem for the Fluidynamic module. Assessment criteria range from Fail (serious conceptual errors, lack of independence) to 29-30 and Honors (complete, in-depth knowledge, critical thinking, originality). Honors (Laude) is awarded for work distinguished by brilliance and originality. To pass, students must demonstrate sufficient knowledge (18-22) with elementary understanding and ability to handle simple tasks.
